headline: Sudarshan Chemical Industries acquisition announcement via NSE Board Meeting outcome notification
sum: Sudarshan Chemical Industries has announced an acquisition, disclosed via NSE Board Meeting Outcome filing on 12 August 2026; specific target and consideration details require access to full disclosure documents.
implication: Listed chemical company M&A in India must be disclosed first via exchange Board Meeting Outcome (BMO) filings; practitioners should verify NCLT approval pathway if target has separate creditor classes, and obtain full disclosure for Reg 30 compliance review.
detail: The acquisition was announced through an NSE Board Meeting Outcome filing, the standard disclosure mechanism for corporate actions of listed Indian companies. Sudarshan Chemical Industries Limited, a speciality chemicals manufacturer, informed the NSE of the Board's decision. Full terms, target identity, consideration structure and regulatory gatings (CCI, NCLT if applicable) are held in the full PDF filing and any supplemental regulatory announcements.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (SEBI LODR), Reg 30
framework.note: Material acquisition must be disclosed to stock exchange within 24 hours of Board meeting decision
Acquisitions affecting competition must file with CCI if consideration exceeds statutory thresholds; applicable to significant chemical industry consolidation

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Sections 230–232 (Scheme of Arrangement) or Section 394 (Merger under IBC)
framework.note: Depending on structure, acquisition may require NCLT sanction if target is insolvent or merger is cross-border
If target or consideration involves non-residents, RBI FEMA approval may be required

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, Part II
framework.note: If target is undergoing CIRP, acquisition must follow IBC resolution process
Board authority for acquisition and any related party transaction disclosures
Acquisition-related trading halts, price-sensitive information windows and related party approval (if applicable) protocols

approvals: NCLT approval (if applicable based on structure)
